title: Critical vulnerabilities in N-able N-central prompt hosted shutdown
content_md: Overview On November 9, 2026, N-able announced that it was responding to the public disclosure of critical vulnerabilities affecting N-central , its remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform. In a public disclosure titled Able2Shell, an independent researcher has published details and proof-of-concept (PoC) code covering 33 issues. According to the disclosure, the issues include unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE), privilege escalation to root, credential disclosure, and unauthorized account creation. One unauthenticated chain combines XML external entity (XXE) and session-handling weaknesses to execute code as the nable service account. Other demonstrated chains involve an administrator viewing malicious patch metadata or use ProductAdmin credentials. Rapid7 Intelligence is currently triaging the newly published details. As of November 10, N-able reported scanning activity associated with the published PoC code and said it had no evidence that any customer environment had been successfully exploited. The vendor has advised keeping N-central deployments offline while it develops and validates a hotfix. Hosted N-central classic environments remain offline, according to the same notice. N-able's notice does not yet include CVE identifiers or CVSS scores. N-central is used by managed service providers (MSPs) and enterprise IT teams to administer endpoints and infrastructure.
